operationsDescription: Review requests and recover files from agent actions.
busyDescription: An operation is in progress or was interrupted. Inspect the recorded locations before taking further action.
purgeDescription: This removes the selected items from trash. Their history remains, but the files cannot be restored through SafeRM.
restoreDescription: Return the item to its original source path.
overwrite: Allow replacement at the original path
overwriteDescription: The occupying item is deleted to recoverable trash before replacement. Confirmation and review rules still apply.
deleteDescription: Move a file or folder to recoverable trash. Review rules still apply.
moveDescription: Move a file or folder to a new path. Its original location is recorded for recovery.
emptyDescription: Agent actions will appear here. You can also move a file to trash or create a reversible move.
filteredEmptyDescription: Change the status or operation type to see more history.
requestFailed: The operation could not be completed
cleanupDescription: Remove eligible history records according to the retention period. Recoverable trash and pending requests are preserved.
cleanupOrphansDescription: Also remove eligible records whose recorded recovery files are missing.

helpSections.title: Review an agent request
helpSections.text: Pending operations appear first. A move can wait for its own review, an occupying delete, or both. Details show its review rule and blocker ID. Approving the delete also executes an unprotected move; a protected move still needs approval. Approve or Deny on a blocked move asks whether to decide both actions. No or closing that question changes neither. Denying or failing the delete denies its pending moves.

helpSections.title: Notification decisions
helpSections.text: Approve or Deny on a blocked move opens a question naming the move and its occupying delete. Nothing changes until Yes; No or closing leaves both pending. After their records are saved, a pending occupying delete sends a notification, and the move sends one only if it remains pending when the command finishes. Immediately completed actions send none.

helpSections.title: Recover a file or folder
helpSections.text: Restore returns an item to its original path. Replacement first deletes the occupying item to recoverable trash. If that delete needs approval, approve it and restore again. Failed operations may also be recoverable; inspect their recorded errors and paths first.

helpSections.title: Create an operation
helpSections.text: Choose New operation, select Delete or Move, and provide a source path and reason. Moves also require a destination. Allow replacement at the destination preserves the occupying item through a recorded delete before moving. The source can remain pending after that delete has completed. Review rules still apply. The GUI asks for replacement consent; only the CLI offers --force to skip that question for move or restore, and force never bypasses review.

helpSections.title: Permanently delete trash
helpSections.text: Select one or more eligible deleted items, then choose Permanently delete. This removes the contents from trash and retains the operation records. It cannot be undone through SafeRM.

helpSections.title: Clean up history
helpSections.text: History cleanup removes eligible records based on the configured retention period. It does not empty the trash. Include orphaned records to remove eligible records whose recovery files are missing.

helpSections.title: Settings
helpSections.text: Edit the trash directory, history retention, and paths requiring review. Valid changes are saved automatically. Move and restore replacement require usable trash to preserve the occupant. Review rules apply independently to the moving source and the occupying delete. Open the configuration file in its default application, or reset settings to defaults.

invalidConfigValue: The configuration file's value {value} can't be used. SafeRM uses the built-in value instead.
malformedRule: A review rule is malformed. Every delete and move needs approval until it is fixed or removed.
